text:
Original BERT4Rec establishes bidirectional masked-item reconstruction, cross-entropy over an output softmax, and appended-[MASK] next-item inference. The paper explicitly includes training examples masking only the last item; these are established practice, although their sampling frequency remains a hyperparameter. A shifted next-item target visible elsewhere in bidirectional input would violate this objective. [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690)

Important code distinction: official `gen_data.py` uses sliding windows and duplicated random-mask reconstruction examples, while `force_last=True` selects the latest window and masks its final item for evaluation. It does not explicitly add last-item-only training examples. The README-used `gen_data_fin.py` does: after random-mask duplication, `mask_last` adds one final-item-only example per training window. Both generators default to `mask_prob=1.0`, so selected targets are always replaced by [MASK], despite inherited 80/10/10 comments. Sliding-window stride defaults to 0.1 × maximum sequence length. [gen_data.py](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data.py), [gen_data_fin.py](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py)

Official `run.py` applies a dense activation plus LayerNorm, tied input/output embeddings, token-specific output bias, and full-vocabulary log-softmax—including special-token rows. `vocab.py` reserves `[pad]`, `[MASK]`, `[NO_USE]`, plus ID 0; generators actually pad with 0 and insert no CLS/SEP tokens. Excluding special tokens from the softmax denominator therefore changes the released implementation. The host baseline still requires separate verification; retain its fixed splits and left-padding contract regardless of upstream preprocessing. [Output head](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py), [Vocabulary](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/vocab.py)
